title: A Bounce Built on Thin Stocks Gave Way
titleLead: A bounce built on thin stocks.
deck: IHSG fell 7.03% to 5,057.050 and gave back the whole of last week's bounce. Foreign selling halved to Rp3.06tn, yet prices fell harder. The 81 stocks leaving the index on 2 November lost more than the rest, and at the same time bond buyers pulled away. We stay defensive.

sections.title: The bounce is gone and we still would not buy it

blocks.text: IHSG fell 7.03% to 5,057.050. It lost 382.208 points, 1.5 times the 254.153 points it gained the week before, and it closed 2.47% below its 16 October level. Compared with the 9 October close the index is down 17.01%.

The usual explanation does not fit. Foreign investors sold a net Rp3.06tn across all stock markets, 54.18% less than the Rp6.67tn of the week before. A week with half the foreign selling should hold up better. It did not. Last week Rp6.67tn of foreign net selling came with a 4.90% rise. This week Rp3.06tn came with a 7.03% fall. Net flows are the same number seen from the buyer's side and the seller's side, so they cannot say who blinked. What moved was the price at which buyers were willing to deal. Everyone also traded less. Total trading fell 29.49% to Rp14.34tn a day, and the biggest fall of the week, 3.49% on Thursday, came on the lowest regular-market value of the week, Rp10.24tn.

The damage was uneven. The 81 stocks that leave the index on 2 November are 28.08% of full market value and 2.34% of regular trading this week. They lost 9.89% of their value against 6.66% for the other 882 stocks, and they account for 35.42% of the value lost by stocks that fell. Four Barito group companies, BREN, BRPT, CUAN and TPIA, lost 21.04% of their value together, about Rp131.7tn, although they had filed buyback plans worth up to Rp3.5tn.

Our view stays defensive, and the reasons are wider than last week's. Last week the question was who bought. This week there is price and funding evidence too. Thin stocks led the fall, the government bond auction drew the weakest bids since November 2024, and two Fed voters wanted a rate increase. We would change our mind when a bond auction draws strong bids again, when foreign selling in TLKM, BMRI and BBRI stops, and when IHSG closes above 5,488 with foreign buying.

blocks.label: Checking last week's call
blocks.text: Last week we said a bounce carried by local buyers had not shown that outside investors trusted the market, and that local money could carry prices for a while. It carried them for four sessions. IHSG is back inside the 4,437 to 5,185 range we called our planning case, near the top of it. Our relief case, which began at 5,488, was never reached. The week's high was 5,453.647 on Monday. We were right on direction. We called buybacks and state buying announced capacity, not proof, and this week supports that caution. The four Barito stocks with buyback plans fell about 21% and the state-owned TLKM fell 11.61%. We still do not know how much was bought.

sections.title: Down on four days out of five

blocks.label: Exhibit 01
blocks.title: Four lower closes and one small rise
blocks.note: Select a date to inspect the closing observation. Lines join daily closes and show no intraday highs or lows.

event.label: The Fed held rates and two voters wanted a hike
event.note: Announced 28 October at 14:00 in Washington, which was 01:00 in Jakarta on Thursday

blocks.text: On Monday IHSG touched 5,453.647, the best level of the week, then closed down 1.22% at 5,373.094. On Tuesday it fell 1.99% to 5,266.130. Wednesday brought a rise of 0.31% to 5,282.312, which was also the high of that day.

Underneath Wednesday's small rise was a strange day. BBCA rose 7.65% and ASII rose 7.99%, while TLKM fell 3.27%. Our estimate of foreign buying in BBCA alone was a net Rp1.20tn, more than the official all-market foreign net buying of Rp665.22bn that day. Thursday undid both moves. IHSG touched 5,320.895 at 09:01, then fell for most of the day and closed at its low of 5,098.057, down 3.49%. BBCA fell 6.35% and ASII 6.20%. Friday added a fall of 0.80% to 5,057.050, after a low of 4,979.342, which was 1.54% below the close.

Trading shrank. Total value averaged Rp14.34tn a day, down 29.49%, and the average number of trades fell 20.99% to 1.54 million. Regular-market value alone averaged Rp12.88tn a day, 28.54% below the week before. Negotiated trades made up 10.18% of all stock value.

By count the fall was broad. 720 stocks fell and only 90 rose. By value it was broader still. Stocks worth Rp7,227tn fell, 82.17% of the value in IDX's chart. IDX again printed the two falling groups' percentages in the wrong order, in both bars. We recompute every share from the counts. Our own count from the stock database agrees: 720 fell, 90 rose and 153 did not move.

sections.title: Foreign selling halved. Prices fell anyway.

blocks.label: Exhibit 02
blocks.title: Net selling on four of five days
blocks.note: Official all-market stock trading, foreign purchases less sales. This measures trading, not money leaving the country.

blocks.text: Wednesday was the only day of foreign net buying, at Rp665.22bn. The week's net selling of Rp3.06tn took the total for 2026 to Rp97.92tn, and this week added 3.12% of it. Foreign investors made up 41% of trading, up from 40%. Domestic investors bought Rp44.02tn and sold Rp40.96tn. Their gross buying was 31.99% below the Rp64.73tn of the week before, so local money also bought less.

Our stock-level estimate covers the 82 liquid large caps with at least Rp10tn of market value and Rp10bn of average daily trading. It puts their regular-market foreign net selling at Rp3.95tn. Five state-owned stocks account for Rp3.37tn of it, or 85.29%. They are TLKM at Rp1.19tn, BMRI at Rp1.13tn, BBRI at Rp507bn, ANTM at Rp288bn and BBNI at Rp250bn. Foreign investors were estimated net buyers of BBCA at Rp411bn and ASII at Rp133bn. Last week BBCA was the biggest foreign sale, at Rp2.95tn. So foreigners eased off BBCA and kept selling the state-owned stocks that rose most last week. The estimate values foreign share volume at each day's close and leaves out negotiated trades. It is Rp1.00tn more negative than the official figure for all stocks, so we use it only to see which stocks foreigners traded.

blocks.caption: Each explanation tested against the evidence that would rule it out

blocks.text: We tested each explanation against the evidence most likely to rule it out. No single cause survives. Foreign selling explains too little because it halved. The Fed explains one day at most. What is left is a mix of bond stress and thin stocks giving way, with shrinking turnover running through both.

sections.title: The stocks that rose most last week fell most this week

blocks.label: Exhibit 03
blocks.title: Eight laggards and two leaders
blocks.note: Official weekly IHSG contributions from IDX. BMRI at -14.35 and EMAS at -11.34 also made the ten largest laggards. The ten largest laggards cost 184.36 points in all.

blocks.text: The ten largest laggards cost 184.36 points, which is 48.24% of the week's 382.208-point fall. The ten largest leaders added only 21.97 points. ASII supplied 10.13 of them, so it was the one large stock that rose. BYAN, BREN and MORA, all on the HSC list, took 65.82 points off IHSG between them. LQ45 fell 5.83%, IDX BUMN20 fell 5.09% and IDX High Dividend 20 fell 2.85%. The index that holds the largest liquid stocks fell less than the index that holds everything.

blocks.caption: Price changes in the stocks last week's argument rested on

blocks.text: This table is the honest scorecard for last week's view that issuer buybacks and state buying might support prices. The state banks kept part of their gains. BMRI, BBNI and BBRI are still 6% to 12% above their 16 October prices. The Barito companies did not. BREN gave back its whole rise and sits 3.23% below where it started. BRPT and CUAN are lower still. The four filed buyback limits worth up to Rp3.5tn between them, and their shares lost about Rp131.7tn of value in a week. Even if every rupiah of the plans were spent, it would equal 2.7% of that loss. We found no report of how much any of them bought.

sections.title: The loss was largest where trading is thinnest

blocks.text: The exit list is now public. Bisnis.com reported on 26 October that 81 stocks leave the IHSG calculation on 2 November, in an IDX rebalancing that runs to 29 January 2027. The stocks stay listed and tradable. Their price moves will simply stop counting. The same report says the index weight of BBCA rises from 8.75% to 9%, BBRI from 7.93% to 9% and ASII from 3.35% to 4.15%. We could not find IDX's own document, so this list rests on the press report. Last week's 80-name list differs by FILM and TFCO added and KING dropped. The count has also moved before. Bisnis.com reported 82 HSC stocks on 23 October.

blocks.label: Exhibit 04
blocks.title: Where Rp764tn of lost value went
blocks.note: Ribbon width is market value lost between the 23 and 30 October closes, by stocks that fell, in Rp tn. Stocks that rose added back Rp38.6tn, so the net change on our share counts is -Rp725.6tn. IDX counts -Rp721tn because it also includes Rp4.6tn of newly issued shares.

rows: Share of regular trading this week
Share of value lost by falling stocks
blocks.caption: Our calculation from daily closes and shares outstanding, using the 26 October list. Changes are weighted by full market value, not by IHSG weight

blocks.text: Last week these 80 stocks lagged the rise. This week they led the fall. MORA fell by 6.79%, 6.95%, 6.76%, 6.87% and 6.97% on the five days, each close to the 7% lower limit IDX applies. It traded Rp3.03bn in total and lost Rp46.3tn of market value, 15,314 times what changed hands. DCII had no trade at all on Wednesday and about Rp17 million on each of Thursday and Friday, and its price stayed at Rp174,975. These prices say little about what investors would pay. When the stocks leave the index, moves like this stop reaching IHSG.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: The exit will help. It is a fair reading of the week to say that thin stocks led the fall. It is not a fair reading to say they caused it. The other 882 stocks lost Rp493.5tn and fell 6.66%, and TLKM, a large and liquid state-owned stock, alone lost Rp25.8tn. After 2 November IHSG will lean harder on banks, the part of the market foreign investors are still selling. The cleaner index removes noise. It does not remove the selling.

sections.title: Every sector fell, and infrastructure fell most

blocks.label: Exhibit 05
blocks.title: Sector index changes over the week
blocks.note: Weekly price changes of the IDX sector indices.

blocks.text: Last week every sector rose. This week every sector fell. Infrastructure lost 13.04%, basic materials 12.23% and energy 10.75%. Healthcare lost 2.02% and financials 2.93%. Our estimate says foreigners sold TLKM so heavily that it made up 89.0% of net foreign selling in the infrastructure sector. The Acceleration Board fell 21.37%, the Main Board 7.47% and the Development Board 6.89%. IDX Value30 lost 2.67% and the sharia index JII lost 9.54%. The more speculative the stock, the worse it did.

sections.title: Bond buyers pulled away and the Fed leaned toward a hike

blocks.text: There were two rate stories. The first is in Washington. On 28 October the Fed kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%, but the vote was 10 to 2. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack wanted a quarter point increase. The statement says inflation remains elevated. Treasury yields lean the same way. The two-year yield ended the week at 4.56%, which is 0.56 points above the top of the Fed's range. A two-year yield above the policy rate usually means investors expect rates to rise. The next meeting is on 8 and 9 December.

blocks.caption: US yields fell over the week and the rupiah weakened

blocks.text: The Fed does not explain Indonesia's week by itself. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.05% on Wednesday and 4.94% by Friday, below where the week began. The Dow rose 0.24%. IHSG had already fallen on Monday and Tuesday. What the Fed result may have done is hit Thursday, when the index fell 3.49% after opening near its high.

The second rate story is at home, and it looks worse. At the 27 October auction of government bonds, bids totalled Rp31.09tn, according to IDNFinancials. That was 52.1% below the previous auction and the lowest since November 2024. The winning yield on the 10-year bond rose 0.30 points in two weeks to 7.54%, which the same report calls the highest in almost four years. The cost of insuring Indonesian government debt against default, the five-year credit default swap, rose from 91.74 on 14 October to 106.35 on 26 October. We read these as lenders asking for more pay to hold Indonesian risk. US yields fell while Indonesian yields rose, so this pressure is local. The Finance Ministry's own auction page would not open on 1 November, so these figures rest on press reports.

Bank Indonesia held the BI-Rate at 5.75% on 21 October and raised its deposit facility rate to 5.00%. Its next board meeting is listed for 17 November. We do not forecast the decision. We note what it faces. The rupiah reference rate ended the week at 18,138, bond investors want a higher yield, and a Fed increase in December would add to both. Raising the BI-Rate would support the rupiah and bonds but cost banks and companies more to borrow. Not raising it leaves the rupiah and yields to take the strain. Higher yields also lower what investors pay for earnings. The market's price to earnings ratio fell from 11.69 on 23 October to 10.76 on Friday, and its price to book ratio fell from 1.45 to 1.32.

blocks.label: Our assessment
blocks.text: Rates are now the larger outside risk for IHSG, ahead of the index reform. A hike in December would meet a market whose bond buyers are already stepping back. The test is the next government bond auction. A weak one would tell us that the problem is the price of Indonesian risk, not just a few thin stocks.

On Monday 26 October IDX and OJK held a press conference. IDX said it met FTSE Russell online on 23 October, and that FTSE Russell kept Indonesia in its Secondary Emerging Market group and did not add it to a watchlist, as its report of 6 October said. That helps, because MSCI's consultation on moving Indonesia to standalone status is still open until 30 April 2027. IDX also said it will tighten trading surveillance and tell the public when it starts an early investigation into suspected manipulation. With OJK it may restrict or pause particular securities accounts during an investigation. It added five independent members to the committee that decides which stocks count as HSC.

OJK said it will extend until June 2027 the period in which companies may buy back shares without a shareholder meeting. It repeated its 2026 enforcement totals. These are fines of Rp2.23tn on 166 parties in cases, late-filing fines of Rp293.78bn on 805 parties and 464 written warnings.

On 28 October IDX's shareholders approved the charter changes for demutualisation. On 30 October IDX launched IDX Commodity 20, an index of 20 commodity-related stocks weighted by free-float market value with a 15% cap on any one stock. Separately, IDX suspended MSIN from 27 October after a large cumulative price fall, according to IDNFinancials.

BBCA had the week's oddest chart. It rose 7.65% on Wednesday on estimated foreign net buying of Rp1.20tn, then fell 6.35% on Thursday. According to IDX's request to BCA, The Straits Times reported on 29 October that DBS had denied a rumour of a merger between one of its subsidiaries and BCA. IDX asked BCA about it that day. On 30 October BCA replied that talk of a merger between BCA and a DBS subsidiary is not true. BCA also reported on 27 October that its nine-month profit rose 4.2% to Rp45.2tn and its loans grew 12.6%. We have no source that links the rumour to Wednesday's jump or Thursday's fall. ASII moved the same way on the same days, up 7.99% and then down 6.20%, and nobody has tied ASII to DBS. A shared cause is at least as likely as a BCA story.

The third quarter reporting season is under way. BCA reported on 27 October. TLKM, BREN and BYAN filed on 30 October, TLKM late that night. We have not read these statements for this edition. Monday is the first session that can price the TLKM report. We also found no new disclosure of how much Danantara has bought, and no new release from MSCI.

blocks.caption: Last week's tests for a durable recovery

blocks.title: The rupiah cost another 0.35 points
blocks.note: The starting values use this week's IHSG and BI JISDOR. Move the sliders to try a different currency assumption. The equity close and the reference rate are taken at different times.

blocks.text: JISDOR went from Rp18,069 to Rp18,138 per dollar, a 0.38% rise. The rough dollar return on IHSG was -7.38% before costs and hedging, against -7.03% in rupiah. The currency made a bad week slightly worse.

Monday 2 November brings the first IHSG without the 81 HSC stocks, and IDX's October inflation and trade figures. Third quarter GDP follows on 5 November, the Bank Indonesia board meets on 17 November and the Fed on 8 and 9 December. A further fall of 2.96% would take IHSG below the 19 October intraday low of 4,907.370. Our planning range of 4,437 to 5,185 still stands, and the bottom of it is 12.27% below Friday's close. A close above 5,488 would not change our view alone. A close above it with foreign buying and a strong bond auction would.

blocks.label: Investment conclusion
blocks.text: We would not buy this bounce or this fall. Large liquid stocks with reported earnings are safer than thin ones, and the HSC exit will make that gap more visible. Until foreign selling in the state-owned stocks slows and the bond market stops asking for more, we stay cautious on a broad recovery.

method: Official foreign trading totals cover all stock markets. Stock-level foreign values are regular-market estimates from foreign share volumes valued at daily closes, for stocks with at least Rp10tn market value and Rp10bn 20-session average daily value. Daily regular-market value and volume in the estimates match all five IDX daily reports exactly. HSC group figures use the 81-stock list reported on 26 October, shares outstanding and daily closes, weighted by full market value. Value lost by a stock is shares times the fall in its close, and only falling stocks are counted. Shares outstanding are held at their 30 October counts, so the totals show price moves only. They are not IHSG weights. Every input is frozen in the HSC comparison file. Breadth shares are recomputed from counts. Index contributions and sector changes are read from rendered IDX pages.
displayMethod: Price returns exclude dividends and costs. Dollar returns use JISDOR and are indicative. Official all-market flows and regular-market stock estimates have different scopes. Exact observations and calculations are available beside the exhibits and in the linked snapshots.
